summary: Brian Boru fuses trick-taking with area control, as players vie for influence over medieval Ireland through battles, church favor, and marriage alliances. It's a tense, somewhat fiddly hybrid where card play determines your options for controlling the shared map.
praised: Clever, unusual fusion of trick-taking and area control
Tight strategic tension with meaningful alliances
criticised: Rules overhead and fiddly bookkeeping across multiple tracks
Can feel swingy or chaotic due to trick-taking randomness
Niche theme that some feel isn't fully realized

interaction.detail: Players directly contest control of regions on a shared map through battles and shifting alliances, while trick-taking hands determine turn strength and options. The map and influence tracks are fully shared, with only card hands kept private.

scoring.how_you_win: You use trick-taking-style card play to gain majority control of Irish provinces while building out marriage alliances and church favor; once the High King condition is triggered, whoever holds the most province control and alliance/favor bonuses wins.

_name: Brian Boru: High King of Ireland
